video_title: Micah Nori Postgame Interview | Trail Blazers 128, Kings 120 | Oct. 23, 2026

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on the Trail Blazers' second-half turnaround
quotes.excerpt: to come out the second half and go on a 15-0 run and really set the tone
quotes.quote: To me was the way we came out the second half. I thought the first half we lost our composure a little bit, started worrying about the refs, myself included. And then we just came out the second half. We talked about it being a five-point game after everything that had gone the way that it had. I think we were four for 22 from three. Donovan had played three and a half minutes and some foul trouble. We were able to sustain with the small lineup and also save Rob some minutes, which was big for us. But to come out the second half and go on a 15-0 run and really set the tone was great, outscoring them 44 to 26.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori credited the Trail Blazers second half turnaround to a 15-0 run and improved composure after a rough start from three. He noted the team was able to sustain momentum with a small lineup to secure the win.

structured.context: Coach Micah Nori discusses the Trail Blazers' second-half comeback against the Kings.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori praises Toumani Camara's defensive impact
quotes.excerpt: I think that his defense obviously late, he goes seven for 12, five for 10, 20 points
quotes.quote: Toumani Camara. I think that his defense obviously late, he goes seven for 12, five for 10, 20 points and I don't think I ran a play for him.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori praised Toumani Camara for his defensive impact and efficient 20-point performance, noting that he did not even run a single play for him during the game.

structured.context: Coach Micah Nori praises the defensive performance and scoring contribution of Toumani Camara.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on the physicality of the small-ball lineup
quotes.excerpt: we're very comfortable I think with the city and Toumani give you a lot of physicality
quotes.quote: We're very comfortable I think with the city and Toumani give you a lot of physicality. And quite honestly, it's not really a post-up league, even though Sabonis is one of the better post-up bigs, but they I think even the one time they were really trying to get it in there late, we were able to get the offensive foul. And we were worried about the rebounding a little bit, but we had to start to gang rebound and I thought that that small group sustained quite a bit.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says the Trail Blazers are comfortable playing small ball because of the physicality Toumani Camara brings, allowing them to effectively defend even against elite post players like Sabonis.

structured.context: Coach Micah Nori explains the team's defensive strategy against Domantas Sabonis and the effectiveness of their small-ball lineup.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on the importance of depth for the Trail Blazers
quotes.excerpt: in this league, you have to have depth all the way through
quotes.quote: I think it's proven that in this league, you have to have depth all the way through and to get seven guys in double figures on a night where we didn't really make shoot well from three, but we get ourselves to the free throw line 30 times and only turn it over 10 times. We trust all those guys and there's even some that didn't get to play tonight that we trust. It just felt like and Danny got Danny played a lot of minutes. The good news is we have three days off for him to recover, but out of necessity, we needed that from him tonight.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori emphasized the importance of roster depth after seven players reached double figures. He highlighted the team's ability to protect the ball and get to the free throw line despite struggling from beyond the arc.

structured.context: Coach Micah Nori highlights the importance of team depth and managing player minutes during the game.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori evaluates Robert Williams III's vertical threat
quotes.excerpt: he always is changing the game, had the one block shot
quotes.quote: He goes six for six, he always is changing the game, had the one block shot. I thought that he came in and again, to have to have him play extended minutes in that first half a little bit was really good. He's a vertical threat, just with his roles. I think that's why you see we go four for 22 from three on I think we were four for 16 on catch and shoot threes. So you just see the gravity of which he pulls, almost like those wide receivers when they're clearing out the top of a zone. We call it for the love of the game route or for the love of the game roll, which is what he was doing and it just it opens up everything.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori explained how Robert Williams III acts as a vertical threat whose gravity opens up the floor for the rest of the team, comparing his role to a wide receiver clearing out a zone defense.

structured.context: Coach Micah Nori explains how Robert Williams III's vertical gravity impacts the team's offensive spacing.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on the team's culture of sacrifice
quotes.excerpt: that's what you've been talking about, right? Sacrifice and not worry about who's on the floor
quotes.quote: I think my favorite scene of the night was I think it was like 28 seconds or so and you were doing your offense for defense substitutions and Damon and Jalen walking off together and laughing and fiving with each other. That's what you've been talking about, right? Sacrifice and not worry about who's on the floor and not that not that anyone gets it right that we get it right. And just the fact that those guys that what that shows you, which is great about this whole ball club is that winning is the most important thing.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori highlighted the culture of sacrifice in Portland, pointing to players like Damon and Jalen happily rotating in and out of the lineup, proving that winning is the only thing that matters to this group.

structured.context: Coach Micah Nori praises the selfless culture of the team after observing players supporting each other during substitutions.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on the team's focus on rebounding and turnovers
quotes.excerpt: the things that we've been harping on the whole year is take care of the ball and rebound
quotes.quote: The things that we've been harping on the whole year is take care of the ball and rebound. We only had 10 turnovers, one of them was my fault on the five-second violation. I never should have taken Rob out. We were small, they switched it that one's on me, so nine for the guys, one for me. But the and then 10 offensive rebounds for them, so that's 20 possessions and we out rebound them and we force them to turn it over 14 times, so with that small unit, which is a credit to these guys and the compete level at which the standard that they set these first two games, that needs to be our habit.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says the team's focus on rebounding and limiting turnovers must become a habit. He took accountability for a late five-second violation, saying that one was on him.

structured.context: Coach Micah Nori evaluates the team's performance regarding turnovers and rebounding against the Kings.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori explains the technical foul situation
quotes.excerpt: Drew felt that he got was getting shoved and not getting any calls
quotes.quote: There's been some pushing both ways and we're small and Drew felt that he got was getting shoved and not getting any calls. And then he ended up shoving Sabonis and then he just jumped up a little bit too aggressively and he was just expressing that he's getting shoved down there too and just to trying to clean it up. So it was pushing and shoving both ways. I mean we shoot 30 free throws, they shoot 30 free throws, so again, we need to just stay composed and it was kind of like any of you Rocky fans out there when telling be cool, be cool and Apollo Creed said that was cool. That was Drew tonight.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori addressed the physical play between Drew Eubanks and Domantas Sabonis, explaining that Eubanks was just trying to express his frustration with the lack of calls on the other end.

structured.context: Coach Micah Nori explains the physical altercation and technical foul involving Drew Eubanks and Domantas Sabonis.
